Description: Transcript has fewer than 6 distinct speech turns for its duration — looks like a monologue or a call that never really started.
Number of back-and-forth turns per minute of call duration is implausibly low (near-silence / one-sided).
Transcript word count implies >210 spoken words/minute sustained — suggests transcript/audio mismatch or spliced content.
Transcript word count implies <45 spoken words/minute — suggests long dead air, hold music, or a mis-fetched recording rather than live counselling.
Lead's turns include natural short acknowledgements/answers (yes/no/okay/numbers) — evidence of a real two-sided conversation, not a read monologue.

Parameter: Prospect asks at least one question
Description: A genuine, engaged prospect usually asks something back (about fees, colleges, placements, process) — total absence across a long call is a mild red flag.
Lead's own name is referenced in the transcript and stays consistent (no other, different lead name appearing) — a mismatch suggests the wrong recording/notes were logged.

Parameter: Personal/discovery detail specific to this lead
Description: Call contains at least one lead-specific fact (board %, JEE score, city, school) rather than being 100% generic script text — generic-only calls are harder to verify as genuinely tailored.
Call duration is broadly consistent with the depth of topics actually covered (e.g. a 20-minute call covering almost nothing, or a 2-minute call marked as covering the full script).
Transcript doesn't end mid-word/mid-sentence in a way suggesting the recording was cut/edited.
Share of total transcript characters contained in long (>200 char) uninterrupted lines is within a normal counselling range, not near-100% monologue.

Parameter: No verbatim block reused across different leads by same associate
Description: Long (~40+ word) verbatim passages are expected script lines, but if an entire transcript is near-identical to another call by the same associate with a different lead, flag for manual copy-paste/fabrication check.

Parameter: Student count claim within canonical range
Description: Stated total enrolled-student figure is close to Kalvium's standard figure (~2,200) rather than an outlier (e.g. 5,000+) that suggests improvisation/exaggeration. NOTE: this regex also catches a partner university's OWN enrolment stats quoted for context (e.g. 'LPU had 5,000 students in CSC') -- treat a fail here as 'verify by listening', not a confirmed violation.

Parameter: University count claim within canonical range
Description: Stated partner-university count is close to the standard figure (~10-12) rather than a wildly different number.
No invented scarcity pressure such as 'only X seats left today' / 'offer expires tonight' that isn't part of the approved script.

Parameter: No invented placement/salary statistics outside script norms
Description: Any LPA/salary figures quoted fall within the ranges normally used in the script rather than an inflated one-off number.
Transcript reflects an actual conversation and is not just ringing tones, a voicemail message, or 'call not connected' content mislabeled as a completed counselling call.
Backend transcription_status is 'success' and transcript_length is non-trivial relative to duration.
Backend audio_fetch_status is 'success', i.e. an actual audio file exists behind this log entry.

Parameter: No signs of a scripted 'demo' recording
Description: No meta-references such as 'this is a sample call' / 'for training purposes' / associate coaching another associate rather than speaking to a prospect.

Parameter: Notes/summary internally consistent with transcript length
Description: The auditor notes/summary do not claim full script coverage while the underlying transcript is extremely short (or vice versa) — inconsistency suggests the summary wasn't genuinely derived from this call.
associate_name field is populated and non-generic.
lead_name field is populated and non-generic.
prospect_id exists and is a valid unique identifier (no blank/placeholder).
audio_recording_url is present and correctly formed (not blank/broken).
call_duration_seconds is present and within a plausible range for a counselling call (not 0 or absurdly small/large).

Parameter: Only one recording per prospect record
Description: This prospect_id is not sharing its audio file with any other prospect_id in the same audit batch.

Parameter: Notes field is call-specific, not boilerplate
Description: notes / script_coverage_summary text reads as specific to this call rather than an identical stock sentence reused everywhere.
Same associate name spelling/casing used consistently for this associate elsewhere in the batch (flags likely data-entry/identity issues, not the associate's fault, but worth cleaning).
None of the required fields (associate, lead, duration, transcript) are empty for this row.

Parameter: Transcript language field present where relevant
Description: native_transcript populated when the call included non-English speech (supports verification against english_transcript).
Associate states their own name.
Associate names Kalvium as the organisation calling.
Associate explains why they are calling (follow-up on an enquiry/form).

Parameter: Confirms speaking to the right person
Description: Associate verifies they are speaking to the actual lead (not a parent/sibling) before pitching.
Associate references the specific form/enquiry the lead had submitted.
Associate asks if it's a good time / requests a few minutes before diving in.
Opening lines vary/feel conversational rather than a rigid word-for-word script read (proxy: presence of natural filler/acknowledgement words).
Associate briefly previews what the call will cover.
Some introduction element is present at all (baseline floor, distinct from quality of intro).
A greeting (hello/good morning/good evening) opens the call.
Associate asks about Class 12 completion status.
Board marks or percentage are discussed.
JEE or equivalent entrance exam attempt/score is discussed where relevant.
Associate confirms interest in CSE/engineering or the relevant stream.
Associate asks about the lead's career goals or reasons for interest.
Associate checks whether parents are part of the decision and includes them appropriately.
Associate asks what other colleges/programs the lead is considering.
Associate asks when the lead plans to decide/enrol.
Associate discusses willingness to relocate or preferred city/region.
Fee range or affordability is discussed without being the sole focus.

Parameter: Discovery questions open-ended, not just yes/no
Description: At least some discovery questions invite more than a one-word answer (proxy via lead response length).
Some discovery/qualification element occurs at all (baseline floor).
The core Work-Integrated B.Tech CSE program is explained.
How the program runs (years, structure) is described.
Associate explains the multi-university delivery model correctly (curriculum consistent across partner campuses).

Parameter: At least one real partner university named
Description: A recognisable, real partner university (e.g. LPU, SRM, JECRC, VIT, Amity) is mentioned by name.
A specific partner-university count is stated (supports E-15/A-15 fact-check).
A specific enrolled/alumni student count is cited (supports A-14 fact-check).
Associate emphasises hands-on coding/project work starting early.
Associate connects the program to current industry/AI-era hiring relevance.
Concrete detail on coding exposure or project-based learning is given (not just a buzzword).
Who teaches / mentors students is mentioned.

Parameter: Fee structure mentioned or offered to be shared
Description: Fees, payment plans, or scholarships are discussed or explicitly deferred to a documented next step.
Associate does not promise guaranteed placement (should mirror the compliant disclaimer pattern: 'we don't guarantee, but train you').

Parameter: Salary/package figures, if given, framed as illustrative not guaranteed
Description: Any LPA figures quoted are framed as examples/ranges rather than promises.
Associate addresses degree validity/recognition when relevant/asked.
Internship opportunities are explained accurately (paid/unpaid status not overstated).

Parameter: No overstated exclusivity ('only program of its kind') beyond script
Description: Claims of uniqueness are consistent with the standard differentiation pitch (see category F) rather than invented superlatives.
Some program-pitch element occurs at all (baseline floor).

Parameter: Pitch tailored to stated interest (not generic-only)
Description: Program explanation references the lead's own stated stream/goal rather than being a fully generic block.

Parameter: Comparison vs. traditional college route made
Description: Associate explains how this differs from a typical B.Tech/college experience.
Associate explains that value comes from the curriculum/program, not the specific campus/college name.
Differentiation is framed around skills and job-readiness, not just brand/ranking claims.

Parameter: No disparagement of specific named competitor colleges
Description: Comparisons are made without unfairly disparaging a specific competitor institution.
Differentiation claims align with the recurring standard talking points seen across the wider call sample (proxy: overlap with common phrasing set).

Parameter: Addresses 'why not IIT/top exam college' objection where relevant
Description: When the lead references a top exam/college ambition, the associate responds to it rather than ignoring it.
Differentiation includes why this preparation matters for an AI-changed job market.

Parameter: No fabricated exclusivity claims ('first and only in India')
Description: Superlative claims, if made, are not contradicted elsewhere in the wider dataset's standard script.
Some differentiation content occurs at all (baseline floor).

Parameter: Balanced tone (confident, not disparaging or exaggerated)
Description: Overall tone of the differentiation pitch is confident and factual rather than aggressive or over-the-top.
If the lead raises a cost concern, the associate responds to it directly.

Parameter: Parental approval objection addressed if raised
Description: If the lead mentions needing to check with parents, associate responds constructively (not pressuring).

Parameter: 'Not a well-known college' objection addressed if raised
Description: If brand/recognition concerns are raised, associate responds with the curriculum/outcomes framing.

Parameter: 'Will I get a job' objection addressed if raised
Description: If job-security concerns are raised, associate responds without over-promising.

Parameter: No pressure tactics used in response to hesitation
Description: Associate does not use guilt, false urgency, or repeated pushing after a clear 'no'/hesitation.

Parameter: Associate acknowledges the objection before responding
Description: Response pattern shows acknowledgement ('I understand', 'that's a fair question') rather than talking over the objection.

Parameter: Objection responses are specific, not deflected generically
Description: Responses address the actual concern raised rather than pivoting to an unrelated script line.

Parameter: Lead's hesitation/questions are not cut off
Description: Long associate turns don't immediately follow a lead question without an intervening answer.

Parameter: No use of comparative fear (e.g. 'you'll be left behind') beyond script norm
Description: Persuasion avoids manufactured fear-based pressure beyond the standard AI-relevance framing.

Parameter: Objection handling present when objections exist
Description: Where the transcript shows a lead objection/hesitation cue, some associate response follows (not silence/topic change).
Associate briefly recaps what was discussed/agreed.
A concrete next step (webinar date, registration, follow-up call) is agreed.
Associate attempts to move the lead toward registration/enrollment interest, per 'Registration/close' scripting.
Call ends with a courteous thank-you/goodbye.

Parameter: Follow-up timing set if not closed
Description: If the lead doesn't commit, a specific follow-up time/date is set rather than leaving it open-ended.
Call does not end mid-topic without any closing exchange.
Transcript shows the lead's own closing response (agree/maybe/decline), not just the associate talking.
Some closure content occurs at all (baseline floor).
This category's automated read is broadly consistent with the pre-existing 'Closure' column value for this call.

Parameter: No contradictory promises made at closing
Description: Nothing promised at closing (dates, guarantees) contradicts what was said earlier in the call.
Associate paraphrases/references what the lead just said (proxy: echoing lead's own words back).
Long associate monologues are not immediately followed by cutting off a lead's short reply (proxy via turn-length pattern).
If the lead repeats a question, associate re-explains patiently rather than showing irritation (proxy: no curt one-word repeats).
Phrases showing empathy/reassurance appear ('I understand', 'no worries', 'that's a valid concern').
No unprofessional language, slang, or inappropriate remarks detected.
Speaking pace (WPM) sits in a natural conversational range rather than rushed.
Associate turns aren't dominated by excessive verbal filler or needless repetition (proxy: repeated-word ratio).
Where native-language segments appear, the associate transitions between English/native language without confusion (checked against native_transcript availability).
Program facts are delivered without excessive hedging/uncertainty ('I think', 'maybe', 'not sure') on core facts.
Positive, energetic framing is used when describing the program (proxy: positive-language density).

Parameter: Lead's engagement sustained to the end
Description: Lead continues responding through to the later portion of the call, not just the opening (evidence call didn't lose the prospect).
No unusually long single lines suggesting extended unscripted silence/hold within an otherwise short call.
No unqualified '100% placement guaranteed' style claim (see E12/G-pattern) that oversteps the approved disclaimer.
No inaccurate claim about degree recognition/accreditation status.
No manufactured urgency beyond genuine deadlines.
No remarks about gender, caste, religion, or similar that would be inappropriate.

Parameter: No misuse of personal data mentioned
Description: No indication personal data is being shared/used outside the counselling purpose.

Parameter: No pressure to decide immediately on payment
Description: Associate does not push for immediate payment/commitment on the call itself.

Parameter: No disparagement of the lead's current school/college
Description: Associate does not belittle the lead's current or prior institution.

Parameter: No inconsistent/contradictory factual claims within the same call
Description: Numbers or claims don't contradict themselves within the same transcript. NOTE: the script legitimately cites multiple different figures in one call (this-year vs last-year cohort size, or a named partner university's own stats) -- a fail here means 'multiple numbers detected, worth a quick listen', not a confirmed contradiction.
No questions unrelated to admissions counselling (financial status beyond fees, personal life probing).
Nothing in the transcript suggests the lead was unaware they were speaking with a counsellor (e.g. impersonation of another role).
